articles.title: Chicago mom accused of killing son enters plea as family sits in courtroom
articles.summary: A Chicago mom accused of killing her 2-year-old son before trying to harm herself inside her suburban home pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder charges.
articles.body: A Chicago mom accused of killing her 2-year-old son before trying to harm herself inside her suburban home pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder charges. With her family sitting in the courtroom, Corie Walsh appeared emotional as she went before a judge for a second time to enter her plea. “They served us with an indictment charging Corie Walsh with three different counts under three different theories of first-degree murder,” Walsh’s attorney, Andrea Lyon, told reporters after the hearing. “We are, as you might know from the last time, very concerned about her mental health and stability.” In her last appearance, Walsh was ordered detained pre-trial, despite her attorneys pushing for medical treatment, saying the Frankfort mother was suffering from a psychotic episode at the time of her son’s killing. At the same time as her hearing, Walsh’s 2-year-old son, Barrett, was being laid to rest. On Thursday, Lyon said Walsh’s family was in court to support her, though none of the family members spoke following the hearing. “Her husband, her mother, her mother’s best friend, a cousin and uncle -- they all support her. They all know this is not about who she is,” Lyon said. Prosecutors did not speak after the Thursday proceedings, but previously argued that Walsh intended to do more than kill her son, but also discussed planning to poison her husband. Prosecutors had previously filed documents detailing what they said happened the day Walsh was found in a bloody bathtub and her 2-year-old son dead in her basement, hanging from a rafter. They revealed that two other children who live in the home, came back from school, saw the situation unfolding and ran to a neighbor for help. The neighbor quickly pulled Barrett down and attempted CPR, but said he had no pulse. He was later pronounced dead at an area hospital. The Will County Medical Examiner’s office ruled his cause of death as asphyxia. An 8-month-old infant was also in the home at the time and had been left on the ground of an upstairs room unsupervised, prosecutors said. Walsh was ultimately found by the neighbor fully clothed, in a bathtub with bloody water, having injuries to her wrist and thighs, prosecutors said. She told authorities at the time she killed her son because “he was the devil” and “anti Christ,” the court docs showed. She later made statements saying she intended to harm her husband when he arrived home, saying she would “poison him with a drink,” prosecutors said, noting that she also believed she had killed her other children as well. She had drinks at home and a number of prescription bottles, they added. Defense attorneys argued, however, that she was in a state of psychosis when she attempted to take her own life and when she made statements to law enforcement and hospital staff. “She was psychotic, and this is not a first-degree murder. This is a tragedy. There are no winners here,” attorney Andrea Lyon said. Prosecutors, citing witnesses, had previously said Walsh had “recently become very invested in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial,” which involved a mother killing her three children before trying to kill herself. The trial generated intense interest for more than a month, deeply dividing the public and drawing attention to issues around maternal mental health after childbirth. Clancy’s attorney said she was suffering from a rare condition called postpartum psychosis. Prosecutors conceded that Clancy had severe mental illness, but insisted she was able to understand and control her actions. According to the court documents, Walsh “had been actively discussing the case via group text message with her friends” up until just hours before the tragic discovery was made inside her home. But defense attorneys said those witnesses also noted some unusual behavior from Walsh hours before the incident unfolded. Members of the group chat described her messages as “confusing” and “out of character.” They said she believed Clancy’s husband killed his children, writing “it was manslaughter, please help I’m really freaking out.” The neighbor who found Walsh also acknowledged she was unlike herself, saying she had dilated eyes and a “weird giggle.” A firefighter and first responder told detectives she was “incoherent” in the ambulance as well. Defense attorneys noted that Walsh saw a counselor recently and had never previously displayed any signs of abuse toward her children, according to family and friends. Despite similarities and text messages surrounding the Lindsay Clancy case, defense attorneys said mentions of Walsh being a “Lindsay Clancy copycat” are “sickening.” “Describing Corie to a copied Lindsay is to take an easy bait,” defense attorney Robert Kerr said. Walsh is expected to appear in court again on Oct. 26.

articles.title: Iran’s president says Tehran wants a deal with U.S. before midterm elections
articles.summary: In an exchange with news organizations, Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian also described meeting twice with the Islamic Republic’s new supreme leader, who hasn’t been seen in public.
articles.body: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Thursday suggested his government was willing to make a deal with the U.S. to end the war before Americans head to the polls this November. “We don’t want it to get to the midterm elections,” Pezeshkian said Thursday in a brief meeting with NBC News and other news organizations on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. “We wish Americans to return to the MOU before the midterms,” Pezeshkian added, referring to a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran that laid out plans for a temporary ceasefire. The agreement, signed in June, eventually collapsed. In response to NBC News’ request for comment, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said: “The Iranian regime has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbors in the region.” “The President is courageously ensuring that such an evil country never possesses a nuclear weapon, which will make the entire world safer and more stable,” Kelly added. Pezeshkian’s comments came two days after President Donald Trump said in a speech to world leaders at the U.N. that he believed the Iranian regime would not make a deal to settle the conflict until after the fall elections. “I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.” Polls show Democrats with an advantage heading into the November contests. The latest NBC News Decision Desk Poll found 31% of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, while another 69% disapproved. Trump on Tuesday also defended the conflict and said he was considering whether to “annihilate” the country or make a deal. Trump has repeatedly said that the goal of attacking Iran was to prevent the development of a nuclear weapon. Soon after the war started, Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which some 20% of the world’s oil flowed before the conflict, sending shock waves through the world economy. In an exchange with news organizations, Pezeshkian said he has met with the Islamic Republic’s new leader twice — including a month ago, for seven hours. Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei assumed the role in early March after his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was killed in an Israeli attack that also killed family members and other senior leaders. Pezeshkian said he did not see “any issues with his health or physical appearance” in their meetings, adding that they sat on the floor on traditional pillows. Mojtaba Khamenei was severely injured in the strike that killed his father, three people with knowledge of the matter told NBC News in July, with burns to his face and body and wounds that have required several operations to one of his legs. Iran’s president briefly addressed other pressing issues affecting the relationship between Tehran and Washington. He said his government was “open” to inspections of its nuclear facilities, which the regime has long maintained is for civilian purposes, and he insisted the regime was not seeking to assassinate the American president. “This has not been the position of the Iranian government that we seek to assassinate President Trump or his family members,” Pezeshkian said. The Justice Department charged an Iranian man in November in an alleged murder-for-hire effort to kill Trump when he was the Republican presidential candidate in 2024. Two others were charged with planning to kill an Iranian American journalist and activist who has criticized the Iranian government over its treatment of women. U.S. authorities said the plot was part of Iran’s efforts to avenge the death of a top Iranian general, Qassem Soleimani, who was killed in Baghdad in a U.S. drone strike Trump ordered during his first term in the White House. Pezeshkian has previously denied an Iranian plot to kill Trump, telling NBC News’ Lester Holt in Tehran last year that the regime would “never” do so.

articles.title: Kyrsten Sinema’s former bodyguard and ex charged after rampage through her home
articles.summary: Former Arizona Sen. Kyrsten Sinema’s former bodyguard and romantic partner was arrested earlier this month in Maricopa County after allegedly breaking into her home and damaging $200,000 worth of artwork and expensive alcohol.
articles.body: Former Arizona Sen. Kyrsten Sinema’s former bodyguard and romantic partner was arrested earlier this month in Maricopa County after allegedly breaking into her home and damaging $200,000 worth of artwork and expensive alcohol. The incident took place on Aug. 30 while Sinema was out of town, according to charging documents. Matthew Ammel, 39, allegedly contacted Sinema and demanded that she post a video to her X account. He told her that if she declined to do so, he would damage a painting every 10 minutes, according to the documents. Sinema told law enforcement officers that she refused, prompting Ammel to take down about 22 paintings and throw them into the swimming pool, according to a probable cause statement. One of the paintings was spray-painted with black lettering and left near the front entrance, Sinema told authorities. She also reported finding shards of glass from broken alcohol bottles scattered throughout her house and inside the pool. Ammel was arrested Sept. 17 after being released from a mental health facility, according to the probable cause document. It was not immediately clear when Ammel entered the facility or why he was admitted. He was charged with aggravated criminal damage and has been released on his own recognizance. Ammel is due to appear in court in early October. It is not clear whether Ammel has retained a lawyer. This is not the first time Sinema and Ammel have made headlines. Earlier this month, a North Carolina judge ruled that the former senator could be sued under the state’s “home-wrecker” law over her relationship with Ammel, who was married at the time of their relationship. North Carolina is one of a handful of states that allow spurned spouses to sue for “alienation of affection” and to seek compensation from a third party responsible for the breakup of their marriage. The law gives aggrieved spouses up to three years to sue. Proceedings are separate from divorces, and jilted spouses must show that the accused “took steps that a reasonable person would expect and did result in the ending of the affectionate marriage between the couple,” according to Cornell Law School. In 2025, a North Carolina influencer was ordered to pay $1.75 million for destroying her manager’s marriage, WRAL reported. Sinema acknowledged the affair but argued she has no connection to the state and cannot be sued there. U.S. District Judge David A. Bragdon rejected that argument, pointing to nine text messages she sent Ammel while he was in North Carolina. The judge said the suit can move forward. The lawsuit, filed by Ammel’s ex-wife, seeks financial damages from Sinema. According to the complaint, the Ammels had “a good and loving marriage” with “genuine love and affection” before Sinema pursued Matthew Ammel despite knowing he was married. Matthew Ammel joined Sinema’s security team after retiring from the Army in 2022. He accompanied her on domestic and foreign travel for several years, according to court records, and was later given a position as national security fellow in her Senate office while he continued to work as her bodyguard.

articles.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico return to White House after judge blocks Trump ban
articles.summary: CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists returned to the White House on Thursday after a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump’s decision
articles.body: CNN, MS NOW and Politico journalists returned to the White House on Thursday after a federal judge temporarily blocked President Donald Trump’s decision to ban the three news organisations, ending days of an extraordinary standoff between the administration and media outlets it had criticised.The journalists were initially denied entry on Thursday morning, with the outlets saying a Secret Service agent confiscated their credentials. They were allowed back into the White House by early afternoon after the administration reinstated their disabled badges.The developments unfolded as Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Washington for talks with Trump, adding urgency to the dispute over access for White House reporters.The three organisations had challenged the ban in a joint lawsuit, arguing that the administration had violated the First Amendment by targeting them over the content of their coverage.Judge temporarily blocks White House banUS District Judge James E. Boasberg Kelly issued a late-night ruling temporarily blocking the White House from enforcing the ban. The temporary restraining order will remain in effect for 14 days while the case receives further consideration.“This is a high bar, but Plaintiffs have met it,” Kelly wrote.The judge said the news organisations were likely to demonstrate that they had not been given adequate due process before their access was revoked. He also said the White House had failed to establish clear standards for conduct that could result in the withdrawal of press access.Kelly described the White House's standard concerning objectionable reporting as “so vague it hardly does the trick.”The judge also rejected the administration's argument that the outlets' reporting posed a national security risk, noting that Trump had initially focused on what he described as negative coverage rather than national security concerns.Kelly was nominated to the federal bench by Trump in 2017. He had also ordered the restoration of access for a CNN journalist in a similar case in 2018.White House says restoring access took timeThe news organisations asked the court for an immediate hearing on Thursday after their journalists were initially denied entry, arguing that the White House appeared to be disregarding the judge's order.The White House said in a court filing that the delay was because it took time to reinstate the journalists' disabled credentials. The administration filed its response shortly after the reporters were allowed back inside.The White House did not immediately respond to emails from The Associated Press seeking comment on the judge's order.Theodore Boutrous Jr., an attorney representing the three outlets, welcomed the ruling.“This is a strong ruling vindicating freedom of the press, due process and the rule of law," Theodore Boutrous Jr. said in an emailed statement. "We greatly appreciate the court’s swift action.”Trump had accused outlets of ‘fake news’Trump announced the ban on Friday, attacking the three organisations as “fake news.” He later argued that their reporting posed a risk to national security.The outlets disputed the justification and argued that the administration had singled them out because of their coverage.During Wednesday's emergency hearing, Boutrous argued that the outlets faced irreparable harm because they were being denied access during a period of major international developments.“We’re at war," he told the judge. "We have world leaders coming to Washington.”Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik defended the administration's position, arguing that the president has broad authority over access to the White House.“Access to the White House is a privilege, not a right,” Velchik said.Velchik also rejected the claim that Trump was engaging in viewpoint discrimination. He argued that Trump had criticised other news organisations without banning them, citing his criticism of ABC as “the worst."Major networks suspend Trump pool coverageThe dispute also prompted other major news organisations to take action in support of the three outlets. The US network press pool, which includes five major networks including CNN, suspended coverage of Trump pool events pending further notice.Kelly's ruling did not address the rotating media pool.Following Wednesday's hearing, the networks continued to withhold footage of Trump unless they received assurances that CNN would be allowed to participate in the White House pool.At Joint Base Andrews, where Trump formally welcomed Xi, journalists from Fox News, CBS and NBC were present but did not shoot video.Crews from NewsNation, Newsmax, Right Side Broadcasting Network, One America News and LindellTV were also present, according to signs displayed on their tripods and cameras.The Associated Press provided its video of Trump's meeting with Xi to its customers so they could decide whether to broadcast it.“We did not stream the coverage on our own platforms, including APNews.com or our YouTube channel,” AP spokesman Patrick Maks said.The AP was among roughly 50 organisations that filed an amicus brief before Wednesday's hearing, urging the court to immediately restore CNN, MS NOW and Politico's access to the White House.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1843, Mexico granted 22,000 acres in California's Cuyama Valley; 183 years later, the largest surviving 5,650-acre piece was permanently protected after a $1 million conservation campaign
articles.summary: The largest remaining intact part of an 1843 Mexican land grant in California's Cuyama Valley has been permanently protected from future commercial
articles.body: The largest remaining intact part of an 1843 Mexican land grant in California's Cuyama Valley has been permanently protected from future commercial development after a successful grassroots conservation campaign. The 5,650-acre Spanish Ranch, managed by the Doiron family, is now protected by a permanent agricultural conservation easement through a partnership with the California Rangeland Trust. The agreement guarantees that the historic cattle ranch will remain working agricultural land forever, preventing future subdivisions or industrial development. The agreement was completed after a $1 million fundraising campaign. It protects important wildlife corridors, native oak forests, and headwater habitats across San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties. According to an official announcement from the California Rangeland Trust, the project protects a continuous farming and ranching tradition that began before California became a state.Preserving a pre-statehood Mexican land grantThe property is the main part of what was originally called Rancho Cuyama (No. 1), a 22,193-acre land grant awarded in 1843 by Mexican Governor Manuel Micheltorena to José María Rojo. After the Mexican-American War ended and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo was signed in 1848, the United States government formally recognized the land grant. Over the past 183 years, large parts of California's historic ranchos have been divided into smaller residential lots, farmland, and industrial sites. Spanish Ranch remains the largest connected parcel from the original 1843 grant that is still being used for agriculture. The Doiron family bought the land decades ago and has operated it as a traditional cattle ranch while preserving its open natural spaces. As development pressure increased in the Cuyama Valley, the family began working with conservation groups to protect the property permanently. In a statement released by the California Rangeland Trust, landowner Pam Doiron spoke about the property's deep historical importance. "The ranch is a symbol that shows that agriculture, history, and conservation go hand in hand," Doiron said. "I am proud, along with my family, to carry that legacy forward."Funding through public and private coalitionsProtecting the land required money from several sources, including federal grant programs, charitable foundations, and individual donors. Federal support came from the United States Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service through its Agricultural Conservation Easement Program. The program provides matching funds to protect working agricultural land. To pay the remaining costs, the California Rangeland Trust launched a $1 million fundraising campaign. More than 140 private donors and seven charitable foundations gave money to the campaign, providing nearly 54 per cent of the project's total funding. A major leadership grant from the John S. Kiewit Memorial Foundation provided the final amount needed to complete the project. According to records published by the California Rangeland Trust, the organization now protects more than 150,000 acres of working land across Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo counties. This represents 34 per cent of its conservation portfolio across the state. Eric Hvolboll, board president of the John S. Kiewit Memorial Foundation, said during a dedication ceremony that supporting conservation agreements for working land fits closely with the region's conservation goals.Safeguard for working landscapes and wildlifeBeyond its historical value, Spanish Ranch provides an important natural buffer between the Los Padres National Forest and the Cuyama River basin. The property offers important habitat for native wildlife, including the California condor, tule elk, pronghorn, and several species of special concern. Under the legal agreement, the Doiron family keeps full private ownership and control of the cattle ranch. However, the easement permanently removes all future commercial development rights. This ensures that the soil, watershed, and vegetation can remain protected. Michael Delbar, Chief Executive Officer of the California Rangeland Trust, pointed to the wider importance of the agreement for protecting land in the region. "Spanish Ranch represents what is possible when landowners, conservation partners, and communities come together around a shared vision for the future," Delbar stated. "We are not just conserving acres, we are helping ensure that these working landscapes remain whole, productive, and connected for generations to come."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: After 59 years at San Francisco's Fisherman's Wharf, Ripley's Believe It or Not! is closing its 400-artifact museum and 2,000-sq-ft mirror maze by year-end and plans to sell several unusual city-linked exhibits
articles.summary: After nearly six decades at San Francisco’s Fisherman’s Wharf, Ripley’s Believe It or Not! is preparing to close its doors before the end of 2026.
articles.body: After nearly six decades at San Francisco’s Fisherman’s Wharf, Ripley’s Believe It or Not! is preparing to close its doors before the end of 2026. The attraction, which opened on February 2, 1967, contains more than 400 unusual artifacts and a 2,000-square-foot mirror maze. SFGATE reported that the company has not announced a specific final date, but the museum will remain open while it organises the closure. Ripley’s also plans to sell several exhibits connected to San Francisco, including a tiny Golden Gate Bridge made on the head of a pin, toothpick versions of the landmark, Joe DiMaggio’s crutches and a chicken-wire portrait of Janis Joplin. The decision ends a colourful chapter in the history of Fisherman’s Wharf, where generations of visitors paid to see curiosities, oddities and objects designed to make them question what was possible.The end of a Fisherman’s Wharf eraRipley’s Believe It or Not! became part of the Fisherman’s Wharf experience long before smartphones, social media and interactive digital attractions changed the tourism industry.For 59 years, the museum occupied 175 Jefferson St., sharing its building with Applebee’s and the Wharf Central souvenir shop. Visitors entering the attraction encountered a collection built around the strange, the surprising and the difficult to explain.The museum’s closing will remove one of the district’s longstanding roadside-style attractions. Fisherman’s Wharf has always depended on novelty, spectacle and memorable experiences, and Ripley’s offered all three under one roof.Its closing is also part of a broader shift in the neighbourhood. Other long-established attractions have disappeared, including Madame Tussauds, which permanently closed its Fisherman’s Wharf location in October 2024.The area is not becoming empty. New restaurants, shops and entertainment venues are planned. But the character of the waterfront is changing, and Ripley’s departure marks the loss of a business that many visitors associated with San Francisco tourism.A museum built around the unusualThe Fisherman’s Wharf museum contained more than 400 artifacts. Some were historic, some were artistic and others were designed primarily to provoke disbelief.Ripley’s attractions have traditionally combined genuine curiosities with unusual art, unusual records, optical effects and stories from around the world. The goal is not to present a conventional museum collection. It is to create a sequence of surprises.The San Francisco location also included Ripley’s Marvelous Mirror Maze, a 2,000-square-foot attraction that challenged visitors to find their way through reflective walls, confusing passages and changing perspectives.A mirror maze depends on a simple idea, but the experience can be surprisingly disorienting. Repeated reflections make it difficult to judge distance and direction, while visitors must rely on touch, patience and careful observation to find the exit.Together, the oddities museum and mirror maze created a family-oriented attraction that appealed to tourists looking for something lighter and more theatrical than a traditional cultural institution.Why the attraction is closingRipley’s has not identified one specific event or problem as the reason for the closure.Suzanne Smagala-Potts, a spokesperson for the company, told SFGATE that Ripley’s had taken a broader look at the attraction, the changing landscape of Fisherman’s Wharf and what made sense for the company’s future. After nearly 60 years at the location, the company concluded that it was the right time to close.That explanation suggests the decision reflects multiple factors rather than a sudden crisis.Tourist districts change over time. Visitor habits shift, operating costs rise and older attractions may need major investment to compete with newer experiences. A location that worked well in the 1960s may not have the same commercial role decades later.The company operates 26 other museums around the world. It also recently closed locations at the Arizona Boardwalk in Scottsdale in August 2025 and in Atlantic City, New Jersey, in 2022.The San Francisco closure therefore appears to be part of a wider evaluation of Ripley’s locations rather than an announcement that the brand itself is ending.The museum’s San Francisco connectionRipley’s history in San Francisco goes back further than the Fisherman’s Wharf attraction.Robert Ripley, the cartoonist and entrepreneur who founded the brand, was born in Santa Rosa. He began working for the San Francisco Bulletin in 1909 before travelling around the world and collecting stories, images and objects that became the basis of his famous Believe It or Not! features.Early versions of the museum appeared at the Golden Gate International Exposition on Treasure Island in 1939 and 1940. Ripley later opened the first official Believe It or Not! location in St. Augustine, Florida, in 1950.His connection with San Francisco continued through later attractions. The city previously hosted the Museum of Witchcraft and Magic at 235 Jefferson St., a venue that eventually became the Guinness World Records Museum. That museum closed in 1994.The history gives the current closure an added meaning. Ripley’s was not simply a national attraction that happened to rent space on the waterfront. San Francisco was connected to the story of the founder and to some of the earliest versions of the brand’s museum concept.Famous visitors over the yearsThe Fisherman’s Wharf museum attracted more than ordinary tourists.According to SFGATE, high-profile visitors included Michael Jackson, former San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown and baseball legend Joe DiMaggio.Celebrity visits added to the attraction’s visibility, but the museum’s appeal did not depend entirely on famous guests. Its main audience consisted of families, tourists, school groups and curious visitors who wanted an unusual experience during a trip to the waterfront.The museum’s location made it easy to combine with other popular activities. Visitors could walk along the wharf, see the sea lions, browse souvenir shops, eat seafood and then step into an air-conditioned world of oddities.That combination of convenience and curiosity helped Ripley’s remain part of the local tourism landscape for decades.Exhibits that will be soldThe closure will give collectors and San Francisco enthusiasts an unusual opportunity.Ripley’s plans to offer several city-related exhibits for sale. The items include a model of the Golden Gate Bridge created on the head of a pin and versions of the landmark made from toothpicks.These miniature works reflect the kind of craftsmanship and spectacle that made the museum distinctive. A familiar San Francisco landmark becomes extraordinary when it is recreated at a scale small enough to fit on a pinhead or assembled from everyday wooden sticks.Other exhibits being offered include Joe DiMaggio’s crutches and a chicken-wire portrait of Janis Joplin. Both objects connect the collection to well-known figures associated with American sports and music.The sale means that some pieces will leave the museum and enter private collections. Instead of remaining together as part of one public attraction, the objects may be distributed among buyers who value their history, construction or connection to the city.Ripley’s has not announced the final sale dates or prices for the exhibits, as per the report.A changing attraction districtThe closure comes as Fisherman’s Wharf continues to evolve.The neighbourhood remains one of San Francisco’s best-known visitor destinations, but tourism patterns and commercial needs are changing. Longstanding restaurants and attractions have closed, while new public spaces, food businesses and entertainment venues are expected to arrive.A new public plaza is planned on the site where Alioto’s once operated. Saigon Sandwich and the local boba chain Little Sweet are expected to open by the end of the year, while Space Karaoke is scheduled to debut in early 2027, as per the report.These additions show that the wharf is not simply losing businesses. It is being reshaped for a new generation of visitors.However, newer venues do not necessarily replace the emotional role of older attractions. A karaoke lounge may draw crowds, but it does not offer the same experience as walking through a museum filled with unusual objects collected over decades.For many visitors, Ripley’s was part of a personal memory of San Francisco. Its closing will be felt most strongly by people who visited as children and later returned with their own families.What visitors can expectThe museum has not yet announced a specific final day. It is expected to remain open sometime before the end of 2026 while the company completes its transition.Ripley’s president, Jim Pattison Jr., said the attraction had delivered the odd, the unusual and the plainly weird during its long run. The company has thanked the Sabella family, the longtime landlords, as well as the hundreds of employees who helped operate the museum over the years.The company has also said it is offering support to team members as they prepare for what comes next.Visitors who want to see the museum before it closes will need to monitor Ripley’s announcements for the final date. Until then, the attraction continues to offer its collection and mirror maze to the public.The closing period may also increase interest in the museum. Some people who have postponed a visit for years may decide to go before the doors shut, while former visitors may return for one last look.A possible return to San FranciscoAlthough the current location is closing, the company has not ruled out a future presence in the city.Pattison wrote that Ripley’s was saying goodbye to this location, but not necessarily to San Francisco. He added that visitors should never assume the story is completely over with Ripley’s.That leaves open the possibility of a new attraction, a temporary exhibition or another format in the future. The brand’s global network and long association with curiosity could allow it to return if the right location and business conditions emerge.For now, however, the Fisherman’s Wharf museum’s run is coming to an end.Since opening in 1967, it has given visitors a place to encounter objects that were tiny, enormous, unsettling, beautiful or simply difficult to believe. Its 400-plus artifacts and 2,000-square-foot mirror maze turned a day at the wharf into a trip through the unexpected.By the end of 2026, the lights will go out on one of San Francisco’s most recognisable curiosity museums. Some of its strangest treasures may find new homes, but the memories created inside the attraction will remain part of Fisherman’s Wharf’s colourful history.You use AI every day. articles.title: JD Vance's H-1B warning to corporate America: We are not going to let you lay off American workers so you can replace them with cheap foreign labor
articles.summary: Vice President JD Vance doubled down on White House's recent action against H-1B visa abuse and put out a message to corporate America: \"We’re not going
articles.body: Vice President JD Vance doubled down on White House's recent action against H-1B visa abuse and put out a message to corporate America: "We’re not going to let you lay off American workers so you can replace them with cheap foreign labor." The message was linked to White House's fact sheet on what the Trump administration has done so far to protect American jobs. The message was nothing new, as the administration recently issued an executive order in which companies sponsoring H-1B petitions will be scrutinized for their employment history -- if they fired Americans and replaced them with H-1B visa holders.Department of Labor's inspector general Anthony D'Esposito shared JD Vance's warning and added: "Lay off Americans to hire cheaper foreign labor? Expect us to come knocking."What has the administration done to combat H-1B abuse?Companies sponsoring H-1Bs will be under scrutiny. The administration will be checked if the companies fired equally skilled Americans and then hired cheaper H-1B visa holders.Last year, the administration imposed a $100,000 fee requirement for some H-1B visa applications. This was struck down by the court but the administration again renewed the requirement.The DHS proposed another H-1B fee that is separate from the $100K fee and this fee is $103, 265. This is not yet implemented.According to White House data, before the 2025 proclamation on H-1B fee, unemployment among recent computer science graduates reached 6.1% and 7.5% for computer engineering graduates – more than double the rates for biology or art history majors. Since the 2025 Proclamation took effect, H-1B registrations filed by the largest IT outsourcing firms have been reduced by 92%, it said.The Proclamation has also caused a nearly 97% decrease in consular processing requests and a shift from lower-paid foreign labor toward higher-skilled and higher-wage workers. The administration also replaced the random H-1B lottery with wage-based lottery.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: After Buck Island spent 20 years removing rats and mongooses, 57 native ground lizards were brought back in 2008; later studies estimated the population had grown to more than 2,000
articles.summary: Discover the incredible success story of the St. Croix ground lizard at Buck Island Reef National Monument, where conservation efforts have transformed the population from just 57 to over 10,000 lizards since 2007.
articles.body: Buck Island Reef National Monument includes the 176-acre uninhabited Buck Island off the northeast coast of St. Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands. It is best known for its coral reef, but it is also now a stronghold for one of the world's rarest lizards, the St. Croix ground lizard. Over roughly 20 years, the park worked to remove rats, mongooses, and exotic plants, making the island safe enough for 57 lizards to be moved there from Green Cay. The Park Service has informally estimated that more than 10,000 lizards live on the island today, although peer‑reviewed studies and Fish and Wildlife Service assessments report considerably lower numbers. The St. Croix ground lizard no longer lives on the main island of St. Croix, where it disappeared in the late 1960s, mainly because of agricultural habitat change and predation by small Indian mongooses, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service reports.Two decades of removing rats, mongooses and exotic plants ahead of the 2008 moveThe National Park Service credits the lizards' success to roughly 20 years of work, ending with the 2008 move, to eliminate nonnative predators and exotic plants. Management reports show that roof rats were eradicated from Buck Island using diphacinone baits. Some literature suggests that this was followed by an increase in the population of house mice. The relocation itself was meant as insurance. As the Park Service wrote in an environmental assessment, the goal was to minimize the risk that fire, flood, hurricanes, tsunamis, or non-native predators could wipe out the lizard populations. To move from endangered to threatened status, the recovery plan requires a self-sustaining population of 500 lizards on Buck Island.57 lizards from Green Cay, 32 females and 25 males, moved in 2008 (NPS cites 2007)The five-year review carried out by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and several scientific articles show that the translocation occurred between late April and early May 2008, whereas the Park Service records it as 2007. The founder group comprised 57 adults, including 32 females and 25 males, taken from Green Cay National Wildlife Refuge. Early results were encouraging. The report indicates that the introduced lizards behaved normally and mated, and that eggs laid by gravid females hatched within two months of the release. Gravid females and juveniles that had not been marked during earlier visits were captured later, showing that the lizards had reproduced on the island within a year.1,473 lizards by 2013, a 26-fold increase, in the Angeli 2018 studyA 2018 study in Ecological Applications by Nicole Angeli and colleagues, including National Park Service staff on Buck Island, put numbers on the recovery. Based on surveys and population modeling, the study estimated about 1,473 lizards on the island in 2013, five years after translocation. The paper tracked the Buck Island population through a series of mark-and-recapture studies and geographic surveys, finding that the population was not only growing but also spreading, with lizards leaving the release area for new territory. A separate 2018 study in Biological Invasions put the pace at 5 to 10 percent growth every six months and projected that the population could grow roughly fivefold before filling all suitable habitat.St. Croix ground lizards showed a population increase and a habitat expansion by 5-10 percent every six months since their translocation to Buck Island, as seen in a 2018 publication in Biological Invasions indexed in PubMed. The population was projected to grow fivefold before colonizing all suitable habitats.More than 2,000 lizards on Buck Island by 2020, against the Park Service figure of more than 10,000A 2020 paper in the journal Oryx estimated about 3,000 St. Croix ground lizards across the four islands where they live, with more than 2,000 on Buck Island. The Park Service's estimate of more than 10,000 is higher than both the Oryx figure and the 2025 Fish and Wildlife Service status review, which puts the total for all four populations at about 2,000, most of them on Buck Island. The Park Service article of June 2020, which appears to be the source of the 10,000 figure, does not explain how that number was calculated. The Oryx authors used a priority-setting method that combined habitat suitability with the presence of, and options for controlling, mongooses to rank candidate reintroduction sites on St. Croix. They found that current land cover would allow extensive range expansion, an increase of 180%, but noted that large-scale mongoose eradication is perhaps unrealistic on a populated island. It is safest to say that the number of these lizards has grown from 57 to more than 2,000.February 2022, 26 lizards moved from Buck Island back to the main island of St. Croix.Buck Island has since become a source for new populations. In February 2022, 26 lizards from Buck Island were relocated to St. Croix, 13 each to the Sandy Point National Wildlife Refuge and the University of the Virgin Islands Wetlands Reserve. Their long-term viability remains uncertain, the Fish and Wildlife Service says, while the Oryx study found that the Buck Island population can support such releases with little risk to the source population. The lizard is still endangered, and all four of its populations face threats from hurricanes, invasions by new species, and other events.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Wangchuk fears 'encounter' after accusing govt of Ladakh atrocities
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said Thursday he feared he could be subjected to an “encounter” for speaking out against what he called
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said Thursday he feared he could be subjected to an “encounter” for speaking out against what he called atrocities in Ladakh, a year after police firing killed four protesters in Leh.Drawing a comparison with Tibet, Wangchuk said Ladakhis had chosen India because of its democracy. “Today, such atrocities are being committed in Ladakh that even China is not doing in Tibet. That is what you are seeing today,” he said, addressing a gathering on the first anniversary of the police firing on Sept 24, 2025.He sought a people’s tribunal to probe the killings, saying a judicial commission set up by Union home ministry had yet to submit its report.“Last year on this day, four people died... Bullets hit their chests, backs, and heads. Those were not pellets that would merely injure you or hurt your eyes. Bullets were fired indiscriminately from automatic weapons, like AK-47s, at the unarmed youth of Ladakh who were peacefully demanding their rights,” Wangchuk alleged.He rejected claims that the protests were triggered by him. He alleged that before the 2020 LAHDC-Leh elections, Ladakhi representatives opposed to holding polls were taken to New Delhi on a special flight and promised statehood and Sixth Schedule status. He blamed “govt failure to honour those promises” for last year’s demonstrations.Authorities imposed curfew-like restrictions in Leh after the alleged “arson and rioting” and subsequent police firing. FIRs were filed and 81 people arrested, including Wangchuk. He was charged under NSA and sent to Jodhpur jail. After 170 days, Union govt withdrew his detention on March 14 this year and he was set free.He feared further action, saying: “They sent me to jail. Inquiries have been made against me. Only an encounter is left. I am ready for that. It is my last wish. Experts tell me that you will be subjected to an encounter. So be it. Let the country wake up, this is my hope.”A complete shutdown was observed in Leh on Thursday, designated as Martyr’s Day. Wangchuk accused authorities of stopping people from attending the rally, a claim denied by police.Police said Ladakh Buddhist Association had sought permission for a public meeting at Leh’s NDS stadium, which has a capacity of 10,000. The administration granted permission for a prayer meet from 10am to noon. Police reported a turnout of 800 at the event and denied allegations that they erected barricades to stop people from reaching the venue.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Get details, communicate govt’s position effectively, PM Modi tells ministers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi is learnt to have told ministers that knowing facts and communicating them effectively was crucial as he asked them to study
articles.body: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi is learnt to have told ministers that knowing facts and communicating them effectively was crucial as he asked them to study issues in detail and put across govt’s position to counter negative narratives.The suggestion came during the two-day Chintan Shivir at a time when issues around Election Commission’s SIR exercise and the IIT-Bombay controversy have become political flashpoints. TOI has learnt that the PM has advised ministers to put across govt’s views during their engagement with people and media in their constituencies. “The message was clear that ministers must have full knowledge of the issues and must be fully prepared to counter other narratives with facts and details,” said person aware of the deliberations at the brainstorming session.All ministers were asked to identify challenges, point out the gaps and suggest action plans for govt schemes to ensure that their intended outcomes are delivered within the stipulated timelines, in the larger interest of beneficiaries. There were detailed presentations under themes, including “Self development along with improvement in functioning of their departments” and “Jan Vishwas se Jan Aadhaar” (trust-based governance to popular support).The session held after a gap of four years is being seen as a mid-term stocktaking exercise to review performance and chalk out strategies for improving overall efficiency of ministers and ministries. Urging ministers to engage with officials at all levels, PM Modi reportedly said it had come to his notice that a minister did not interact with officials below the secretary in the department while suggesting that interaction with officials of levels was necessary for better performance.PM, in his brief address, has asked ministers to ensure saturation of around 40-45 major welfare schemes and communicating their benefits effectively to the intended beneficiaries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger helped raise €1.3 million for environmental projects in 2026; Wild Solutions Park is restoring habitats in Austria
articles.summary: Arnold Schwarzenegger helped raise €1.3 million for environmental and climate protection initiatives at a special dinner in Kitzbühel on 22 January 2026,
articles.body: Arnold Schwarzenegger helped raise €1.3 million for environmental and climate protection initiatives at a special dinner in Kitzbühel on 22 January 2026, according to the Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative. More than 170 guests attended the event at the Stanglwirt, where an auction featured artworks, signed memorabilia, exclusive experiences and personal collectables, including a private workout with Schwarzenegger and one of his watches. The proceeds will support selected environmental projects worldwide. The fundraiser comes as Schwarzenegger’s Climate Initiative is involved in the Wild Solutions Park in Asparn an der Zaya, where wild horses and hardy cattle are being used to create habitats for endangered animal and plant species while supporting biodiversity, climate action and research.How did Arnold raise €1.3 million for climate projectsThe Special Dinner for Climate Action featured a range of items and experiences connected to Schwarzenegger and other public figures. Among the auction highlights were a private workout session with Schwarzenegger, VIP and meet-and-greet packages, and one of his watches, according to the Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative.The organisation said the evening raised €1.3 million for environmental and climate protection initiatives. More than 170 people attended, including Schwarzenegger’s son Christopher Schwarzenegger, ski legend Franz Klammer, Italian athlete Dominik Paris, footballer Mario Gomez, actor Mark Keller, The BossHoss and Ralf Möller. The Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative said the money raised would support selected projects worldwide.What did he say about taking action for the environmentThe event was held at the Stanglwirt in Kitzbühel, where Schwarzenegger addressed guests about the need for action on environmental issues. According to the Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative, he linked the qualities associated with the Hahnenkamm Race courage, speed and determination with the need to address pollution and take responsibility for the environment.Schwarzenegger also encouraged individuals to consider what they could do in their everyday lives. The Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative quoted him as saying: “You don’t have to be perfect to make a difference. Often, it is enough to ask yourself: How can I be useful right now, and what can I do to make the situation better?” He also called on people to take responsibility and set an example through small actions.What is the Wild Solutions Park working to achieveThe fundraising event comes as the Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative is also involved in the Wild Solutions Park in Asparn an der Zaya, in the Leiser Berge Nature Park. According to the Wild Solutions Park, the project is developing a landscape focused on biodiversity, climate action and regional development.The park uses wild horses and hardy cattle breeds to help create new habitats for endangered animal and plant species. The Wild Solutions Park said bison and water buffalo may also be introduced in the future. The project describes itself as an initiative where nature, agriculture and research work together, while also providing opportunities for schools, universities, businesses and visitors to learn about approaches to environmental management.Solution park approach to biodiversity and climate challengesThe Wild Solutions Park is a joint project involving the Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative, the Austrian World Summit – Solutions Hub, the Regional Development Association (REV) – Leiser Berge Nature Park, MAMUZ Asparn and Green Bridge GmbH, according to the park's website.The project began as a pilot initiative and is being developed as a place for conservation, learning, research and regional development. Its work includes the use of animals and living soils to create habitats and explore approaches to the sustainable use of the landscape. The park said its wider aim is to demonstrate how nature, agriculture and research can work together in addressing biodiversity and climate-related challenges.You use AI every day. articles.body: Turkish businessman Turhan Mildon, CEO of Miller Holding and vice chairman of Turkish football club Çorum FK, is in the spotlight after reports that he is set to marry Alina Habba, US President Donald Trump’s former personal lawyer and adviser.The couple is scheduled to marry in New York on September 26, according to Türkiye Today. Mildon has confirmed the relationship and said the couple met in the US through a mutual friend who was an ambassador. He also rejected speculation that their marriage had a political purpose, saying: “This marriage has no political purpose.”Who is Turhan Mildon?Mildon is a third-generation member of the family behind Miller Holding, a Turkish business group with interests including construction, mining, energy and international investments. The company identifies him as its CEO and describes him as part of its third generation of family leadership.Miller Holding was established in 1967 by Muhsin Turhan Mildon and subsequently expanded into several sectors. Under its current leadership, the group has focused heavily on international projects, particularly in Africa.Mildon's official company profile says he has been involved in projects spanning public investments, healthcare complexes, residential developments, logistics centres and infrastructure. The company's corporate material also highlights its work in Africa and its international expansion.Mildon is also associated with football in Turkey. He serves as vice chairman of Çorum FK, while the wider business group has investments connected to football in Africa. Miller Holding has highlighted the success of Vita Club in the Democratic Republic of Congo, including its Congo Cup victory.Third marriage for AlinaAlina Habba married lawyer Matthew Eyet in 2011. They divorced in 2019 and have two children, Chloe and Luke. Eyet was also her law-firm partner; the firm Sandelands Eyet LLP was formed during their marriage.Habba married businessman Gregg Reuben in 2020. Reuben is the founder and CEO of Centerpark, a parking-management company. Their divorce was finalized in early 2026. They did not have any children.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Saudi foreign minister warns Houthi threat goes global as Trump holds fire
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles as Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud urged global action to protect Red Sea shipping routes.
articles.body: UNITED NATIONS — Saudi Arabia's foreign minister warned Thursday that the growing threat from Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis extends far beyond his country's borders, calling for international cooperation to protect critical shipping routes after Saudi forces intercepted six ballistic missiles launched toward the kingdom. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud told Fox News Digital that Riyadh was coordinating with Washington and other international partners as Houthi attacks threatened Saudi territory and commercial shipping in the Red Sea. The Saudi-led coalition said Thursday that its air defenses had intercepted six ballistic missiles allegedly launched by the Houthis toward the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu, according to Reuters. It was not immediately clear whether the attacks caused casualties or damage. AMERICANS WARNED AGAIN TO RETHINK TRAVEL AS MISSILE ATTACK RATTLES HISTORIC REGION Saudi authorities also issued emergency warnings across several areas, including Jeddah and Mecca, before announcing that the immediate danger had passed. Yanbu, a major Red Sea oil export hub, has become particularly important as the war with Iran disrupts shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Asked by Fox News Digital whether Saudi Arabia was receiving the support it needed from the US following reports that President Donald Trump had declined Saudi requests for direct military intervention against the Houthis, Prince Faisal emphasized the kingdom's ability to defend itself while calling for a broader international response. "So we are, of course, defending ourselves. And we are responding as necessary to the attacks by the Houthis. But we are also, of course, coordinating with all of our international allies, because this is not just about Saudi Arabia," he said. IRAN’S PROXY MONEY MACHINE: HOW THE HOUTHIS BUILT A MULTIBILLION-DOLLAR NETWORK DESPITE US SANCTIONS "The fact that the Houthis are threatening the Bab el-Mandeb, threatening international shipping, is a risk to international security stability. That means that the responsibility to dealing with this threat is not just on Saudi Arabia, it is also on the whole international community." The foreign minister thanked countries already working with Riyadh and confirmed that discussions with Washington were continuing. "And we are obviously continuing to work with our partners in the U.S., to address the issue of this conflict as well," he said. HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS His remarks came as the Trump administration faced renewed requests from Saudi Arabia to take military action against the Houthis. According to a Sept. 21 Axios report, Trump considered ordering strikes against the group over the weekend but ultimately decided against them. The report said Saudi officials had again sought American military assistance as Houthi forces advanced in Yemen, while the U.S. continued providing intelligence and targeting support without directly entering the fighting. The Houthis' territorial advances have intensified concerns over control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic passage connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and a crucial route for international trade and Saudi oil exports. articles.title: ‘No greater partner than President Trump’: Netanyahu defends Iran war, attacks critics as delegates walk out at UNGA
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used his address to the 81st United Nations General Assembly on Thursday to defend Israel’s military actions
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu used his address to the 81st United Nations General Assembly on Thursday to defend Israel’s military actions against Iran and Hamas, praise US President Donald Trump and attack critics including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.Netanyahu’s speech was marked by a walkout by dozens of delegates as he took the podium. He responded by calling those who left “moral cowards” and continued his address to a hall in which many seats were visibly empty. Supporters in the viewing gallery cheered and applauded Netanyahu during parts of the speech.‘No greater partner than President Trump’Netanyahu strongly praised Trump for his support of Israel and said the two countries had acted together against threats posed by Iran."In this battle against the barbarians, we've had no greater partner than President Trump. I thank him for his bold leadership. He boldly confronted an enormous danger to America, Israel, and the world...Israel and America acted together, not only to protect ourselves, but to save civilization," Netanyahu said.He also credited US-Israeli cooperation for Israel’s military campaign against Iran, saying the two countries had acted to protect themselves and the wider world.Netanyahu calls Iran strike ‘one of the easiest decisions’Defending Israel’s military action against Iran’s nuclear facilities, Netanyahu said the decision to launch the operation had been difficult but necessary for Israel’s security."...Devastating Iran's nuclear facilities was hard. It was very hard to do. But for me, it was one of the easiest decisions I've ever had to make as prime minister. Because if we hadn't done it, we'd all be dead. Now, you want to hear the ultimate irony? In defending itself, Israel is also defending many of the countries whose delegates just left this hall. Many of their leaders even thank us privately for taking out Iran's nukes. It's hard to imagine more mind-blowing hypocrisy, but that's exactly what it is," he said.The remarks came amid continuing tensions over Israel’s military campaign against Iran. Netanyahu has repeatedly framed the operation as an effort to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapons capability.‘Seven-front war’: Netanyahu lists Israel’s adversariesNetanyahu described Israel as having fought what he called a “seven-front war” over the past three years, listing Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, Iran, Iran-backed militias in Iraq and Syria, and Palestinian militants in the West Bank."For the past three years, our heroic soldiers have fought day in and day out in a seven-front war. Do you know any other country the size of New Jersey, capable of fighting a seven-front war? Seven fronts – Hamas, Hezbollah, the Houthis, Iran, militias in Iraq, militias in Syria, Palestinian terrorists in Judea and Samaria; they all ganged up on us to wipe us off the face of the earth," he said.Netanyahu said Israel had responded by launching military operations against those groups."They failed. Because instead of collapsing, we delivered crippling blows to all of them. With our great American friends, we crushed Iran's army, navy, air force and nuclear facilities. Israel hammered Hamas. We pummeled Hezbollah," Netanyahu added.Netanyahu holds up pager while referring to HezbollahDuring his speech, Netanyahu held up a pager while referring to Israel’s 2024 operation against Hezbollah. He said the group’s leadership had suffered major losses and referred to the pager explosions that targeted members of the Iran-backed group in Lebanon and Syria.“You remember the beepers? Remember these things? Remember them? Well, I can tell you this: Hezbollah certainly remembers them...Hezbollah's leaders, dead. Their spirit, broken. The arch terrorists, the worst mass murderers on earth, not only killing Israelis, killing Americans, killing Brits, killing citizens of hundreds, dozens of countries...They're all gone too. The remaining terrorists are desperately trying to regroup. Every day, they try to murder our people. And in particular, they try to murder our people in our historic homeland, in Judea,” the Israeli PM said.The pager attack in September 2024 involved remotely detonated pagers used by Hezbollah members and killed and wounded people across Lebanon and parts of Syria.Netanyahu rejects colonialism accusationsNetanyahu also defended Israel’s territorial policies and rejected accusations that Israel was pursuing colonialism. He invoked Jewish historical ties to the Golan Heights while criticising countries including Britain and France."...We weren't in Gaza. We weren't on the Golan Heights. The Jews have been on the Golan Heights since the days of Moses. You can read it in the Bible. On the eve of the Six-Day War in 1967, we weren't in any of these places. We were in a tiny sliver of land. We still are. That is equal to about one-third of 1 % of the landmass of the entire Arab world. Yet they accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism, some colonialism. And who's accusing us? Well, among them are people in Britain and in France...Colonialism gave us a break. Another lie,” Netanyahu further said.Netanyahu attacks Qatar and ErdoganNetanyahu accused Qatar and Turkey of spreading what he described as false narratives about Israel and criticised their relations with Hamas."Several foreign countries have spent untold billions to spread lies about my country. The first to do so was Qatar...Their goal was clear. Brainwash young minds to hate Israel, hate America, hate the West. This is the same Qatar that hosts the Hamas butchers of October 7th. Now the latest country to become a super spreader of anti-Semitic lies is Turkey. Erdogan is a tyrant. He also hosts the Hamas terror chiefs. He's murdered thousands of Kurdish civilians. He denies the Armenian genocide. He jails journalists and opposition leaders. In fact, I think he holds the world's record on this, and that's a tough call. But I think he's number one," he said.Netanyahu clashes with Mamdani over Gaza allegationsNetanyahu devoted part of his address to Mamdani, accusing the New York mayor of contributing to an environment in which Jewish residents feel unsafe and of associating with people who have expressed support for Hamas."Mr. Mamdani, since you were elected mayor of this city, many Jews no longer feel safe in New York. They talk to me. They tell me, “This isn't the city we remember. It changed so quickly.” You praise criminals convicted of supporting Hamas. You count as friends people like Hasan Piker, who said America deserved 9/11. “America deserved 9/11.” Some friends you have. You invited to your home a Palestinian journalist who filmed Hamas terrorists beating and torturing Israeli hostages, and later admitted that he refused to publish the videos in order to protect, you guessed it, the terrorists," he further said.He also accused Mamdani of attempting to prevent him from attending the UN and rejected allegations that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza."Your wife liked a post praising the October 7 massacre. She liked another post saying Tel Aviv shouldn't exist. You refuse to condemn any of that. You falsely and repeatedly accuse Israel of genocide. Mr. Mamdani, you try to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth. And here's the simple truth. Here's a simple truth: Israel didn't commit genocide; Israel prevented genocide," he said.Mamdani has repeatedly criticised Netanyahu’s conduct of the Gaza war and previously referred to him as a “war criminal”. He has also disputed Netanyahu’s characterisation of his criticism of Israel as antisemitism.Dozens of delegates walk out as Netanyahu begins speechThe Israeli prime minister’s address began with a visible protest inside the General Assembly hall, with dozens of delegates walking out as he approached the podium. The chair repeatedly called for order as Netanyahu began speaking.Netanyahu directly addressed those who had left, saying: "Before I begin, just a quick announcement: if there are any other moral cowards who haven’t yet left this hall, please do so now. Thank you very much."He later argued that Israel’s actions against Iran had also benefited countries whose representatives had walked out, claiming some foreign leaders had privately thanked Israel.Netanyahu urges Jews to ‘raise your head high’Netanyahu also spoke about what he described as rising antisemitism and called on Jews around the world to remain confident in the face of threats."The anti-Semites of the world want to terrify our people. I have news for them: the days when Jews were defenseless victims, marched to the slaughter, those days are over. Today, we have a state. Today, we have an army. Today, we have a people ready and willing to defend ourselves. Today I have one message for Jews around the world: raise your head high, be proud, be confident, don't be intimidated. Stand up. Everyone else who wants to defend truth and justice, join us in standing up to the barbarians who threaten our common civilization,” he said.Netanyahu’s address combined a defence of Israel’s military campaigns with attacks on international critics, while placing the US-Israel partnership and the confrontation with Iran at the centre of his message. Supporters in the viewing gallery gave him a standing ovation at the conclusion of his speech.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
